"I will NOT be a human septic tank."

I said that out loud to myself in the bathroom mirror at 6am on a Tuesday. 9 days. No bowel movement. Stomach so distended I had to unbutton my pajamas to breathe. Down 14 pounds on Wegovy and terrified to step on the scale because I had no idea anymore how much of me was actually me, and how much was just trapped food from the last week and a half.

I leaned on the sink. The tile was cold. My face in the mirror did not look like my face. The skin under my eyes was gray.

I had been on Wegovy for 11 weeks.

Knees stopped hurting. Jeans fit. People at church asking what I was doing.

And every meal I had eaten in the last 9 days was still inside me, fermenting, waiting, refusing to move.

I told myself in the mirror that morning I was going to figure out what was actually happening to me. Even if my doctor would not.

The 9 days had a shape to them.

Day 2 I cancelled lunch with Carla. I told her I had a migraine. The truth was I could not sit at a restaurant table for an hour with my jeans unbuttoned under the napkin.

Day 4 I stopped eating dinner. Not because I was not hungry. Because by 4pm my abdomen was so distended I could press my fingers into it and they would not give. The thought of putting one more bite of food on top of what was already trapped inside me made me cry into my plate.

Day 5 I missed my granddaughter Hazel's piano recital. She was playing "Heart and Soul" for the first time. I was at home in the recliner because lying flat made the pressure under my ribs unbearable. My daughter sent me the video. I could not watch it for 3 days.

Day 6 my husband Roy stood at the foot of the bed and asked me what was actually going on. I told him. He sat down on the edge of the mattress and was quiet for a long time. Then he said, "Linda. This is not a side effect. This is something else."

Day 7 I went to my GI. She told me to take Miralax twice a day. Add Colace. Drink a gallon of water. "This is just a side effect. Stay on top of it." I had been on Miralax for 6 weeks already. I had already started doubling. I told her that. She said I could stay on Miralax indefinitely. It was perfectly safe. I drove home with another bottle in the passenger seat.

Day 8 I started cancelling things on my calendar 2 weeks out. I did not want to commit to anything I might not be able to attend.

Day 9 was the mirror.

That night I called my sister Marlene.

4 years older. Retired postal carrier. Not a nurse. Not a doctor. The most stubborn woman I have ever known.

I told her everything. The 9 days. The Miralax. The recital. The mirror.

There was a long pause. Then quietly: "Linda. I'm going to figure this out."

She hung up.

2 nights later my phone buzzed at 11:40pm. A text from Marlene.

"Linda. I have been on Reddit for 4 hours. You are not crazy. You are not alone. I have pulled the same sentence you said into your mirror out of 60 different women's posts."

Then she sent screenshots.

"I will not be a human septic tank."

"My abdomen feels like a brick by 4pm."

"I'm scared to weigh myself."

"Every meal I've eaten this week is still inside me."

The same sentences. Almost word for word. From women I had never met.

I read them in bed at midnight and I cried into the pillow so I would not wake Roy.

2 nights after that she called me at 8pm. I picked up on the first ring.

She did not say hello.

She said, "Linda. I figured out what the medication is actually doing. The appetite part. The part making you eat less. That happens in your brain. That's the engine of your weight loss. Don't touch that part."

I said okay.

She said, "But there's a second thing nobody told you. The medication takes your stomach from normal to nearly frozen. Food that should leave in 4 hours sits there for 10 or 12. Bacteria ferment it. That is where every symptom you have is coming from. Not your colon. Your stomach."

I sat down on the edge of the tub.

She said one more thing before she hung up.

"Linda. There's a plant compound called apigenin. It works on the stomach wall. Most products selling it are powder, not standardized extract. The dose is wrong. I'm still reading. I'll call you Saturday."

She hung up.

That Saturday I drove the 90 minutes to her house.

We sat on her back porch. She had a sweating glass of iced tea on the railing. She told me she had ended up on a thread on a private GLP-1 forum where 3 different women in their 60s had each named the same product. Each one independently. None of them knew each other.

A small company called Motilli.

Heart-shaped celery juice gummies. 2 a day. Standardized apigenin extract from celery. Not powder. Combined with chlorophyllin and a small targeted dose of soluble prebiotic.

The 3 women had each been on a GLP-1 for over a year. Off Miralax for months. Bloating gone. Eating dinner again.

Marlene told me she had ordered a bottle the night before I came over. Not for me. For herself. Because she had decided after 4 nights of reading that if I ever went on a GLP-1 again after this, she was not letting me start without it on the counter.

She said, "Linda. I'm not a doctor. I'm your sister. But I have spent 4 nights of my life reading about your bowels and I am telling you, the women who are clearing this are clearing it with this."

I sat with that for a while. The wind moved the wind chimes on her porch.

I drove home that afternoon and ordered a bottle from my own kitchen.

Here is what I had figured out by then, in my own words, because Marlene had been priming me over a week of calls.

The medication is doing 2 separate things to my body. Not 1.

The first one is happening in my brain. The appetite suppression. The part that makes me eat less. That is the engine of the weight loss. The 14 pounds. The knees. The jeans. I do not want to undo that part.

The second is happening in my stomach. Not my colon. My stomach.

The medication has taken my stomach from normal to nearly frozen. Food that should leave in 4 hours is sitting there for 10 or 12. While it sits there, bacteria ferment it. That is where the bloating, the pressure under my ribs by 4pm, the feeling of food rotting inside me, all of it, is coming from.

I am not constipated. I am backed up at the top. Those are 2 different things.

Every product my GI had told me to take. The Miralax. The Colace. The magnesium. The fiber. Every single one works on my colon. 6 feet downstream from where the actual problem is sitting.

The food was still trapped at the top. Miralax could not reach it. That is why it worked while I was taking it. That is why the second I stopped, I was right back where I started.

And every week I kept taking it, my body was forgetting how to move on its own.

The medical term for that is laxative dependency. Women on daily Miralax for 1 year, 2 years, 5 years, ending up with bowels that will not move at all. Some hospitalized for partial obstructions.

I had been on daily Miralax for 6 weeks. I had already started doubling. I had felt my body getting used to it.

I had not had the words for any of it until Marlene started feeding them to me one phone call at a time.

The bottle arrived 3 days after I ordered it.

Days 1 through 4, nothing. Day 5, the 4pm pressure was not as sharp. Day 7, Roy said at dinner my face looked normal again. Day 9, I went on my own. No Miralax. I sat on the edge of the tub and could not remember the last time my body had done that without me forcing it. Day 14, a full plate of pasta with Roy and his brother. 3 hours later on the couch, laughing at a movie, not thinking about my stomach once. Week 3, Hazel was over. We made cookies. I ate 2. Week 4, I took the Miralax, Colace, magnesium, fiber gummies, and psyllium husk off my counter and put them in a trash bag. Week 6, Roy walked into the kitchen, saw the empty counter, and said, "Took you long enough."

I am not affiliated with the company.

Motilli runs a 90-day money-back guarantee. The bottles sell out for stretches because apigenin degrades from light and heat, so they batch-produce. If you have a vacation, a holiday, a wedding coming up, I would not wait until next week.

If you have been saying "I will NOT be a human septic tank" in your own bathroom mirror at 6am, I hear you. None of it is in your head. Your body is telling you something your doctor is not.

The link is below.

P.S. Marlene started Wegovy herself 5 weeks ago. She has been on Motilli since day 1. She told me on the phone last Sunday that she has not had a single bad day. She said she spent 4 nights staying up for me and 0 nights staying up for herself, and that was the trade she would make every time. The link is below.
